MOBILE CLINIC PILOT - CONTRACTORS WILL BE SELECTED VIA AN RFP PROCESS TO SUPPORT THE PURCHASE AND ONGOING STOCKING OF EIGHT MOBILE HEALTH VANS, WHICH WILL BE USED TO PROVIDE PREVENTATIVE CARE, WELLNESS CHECKS, DISEASE MANAGEMENT, DENTAL CLEANING, AND/OR APPLICABLE SERVICES IN RURAL AREAS. FORMALIZE MEDICATION ADMINISTRATION TRAINING THROUGH THE STATE’S COMMUNITY COLLEGES. E. name: KANSAS HEALTH INSTITUTE
description: THE PURPOSE OF THIS SUPPORT IS TO ASSIST ORGANIZATIONS APPLYING FOR FUNDING UNDER THE RURAL HEALTH TRANSFORMATION PROGRAM (RHTP) BY PROVIDING TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO DEVELOP AND SUBMIT APPLICATIONS THAT ALIGN WITH ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA, CLEARLY AND EFFECTIVELY ARTICULATE THEIR VISION, AND DEMONSTRATE FEASIBLE APPROACHES TO IMPLEMENTATION. THIS SUPPORT ALSO AIMS TO STRENGTHEN THE OVERALL QUALITY AND COMPLETENESS OF APPLICATIONS, ADDRESS QUESTIONS OR GAPS THAT ARISE DURING THE APPLICATION PROCESS, AND SUPPORT CURRENT GRANTEES IN MEETING REPORTING REQUIREMENTS AND DOCUMENTING PROGRESS, OUTCOMES AND LESSONS LEARNED. KHI ALSO WOULD WORK WITH KDHE TO IDENTIFY OPPORTUNITIES TO IMPROVE AND STREAMLINE RFPS AND THE APPLICATION PROCESS BASED ON APPLICANT QUESTIONS, RECURRING CHALLENGES AND LESSONS LEARNED THROUGH TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE. A CORE COMPONENT OF THIS WORK IS TO ASSIST GRANTEES ONBOARDING WITH BDO AND SERVING AS A HELP DESK, PARTICULARLY FOR FIRST-TIME GRANTEES. THE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE HUB IS DESIGNED NOT ONLY TO RESPOND TO INDIVIDUAL QUESTIONS, BUT ALSO TO STRENGTHEN THE KNOWLEDGE AND CAPABILITIES OF APPLICANTS AND GRANTEES TO SUCCESSFULLY PARTICIPATE IN RHTP. KHI WILL USE INDIVIDUAL INTERACTIONS TO IDENTIFY RECURRING KNOWLEDGE, SKILL AND IMPLEMENTATION NEEDS; TRANSLATE THOSE NEEDS INTO TRAINING, TOOLS AND OTHER BROADLY AVAILABLE RESOURCES; AND USE LESSONS FROM THOSE ACTIVITIES TO CONTINUOUSLY IMPROVE SUBSEQUENT TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE. THROUGH THIS CYCLE, INDIVIDUALIZED ASSISTANCE AND PROACTIVE EDUCATION WILL REINFORCE ONE ANOTHER AND BUILD THE CAPACITY OF PARTICIPATING ORGANIZATIONS TO ADDRESS SIMILAR NEEDS INDEPENDENTLY OVER TIME.

name: COUNTY OF ESMERALDA
description: ESMERALDA COUNTY WILL ESTABLISH THE FOUNDATION OF A COORDINATED, SUSTAINABLE COUNTYWIDE EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES (EMS) SYSTEM THAT IMPROVES TIMELY ACCESS TO EMERGENCY CARE FOR RESIDENTS, VISITORS, AND THE REGIONAL WORKFORCE. DURING THE PROJECT PERIOD, THE COUNTY WILL TRANSITION FROM A PRIMARILY VOLUNTEER-BASED EMS SYSTEM TO A HYBRID MODEL SUPPORTED BY FULL-TIME EMS PERSONNEL, 24/7 PARAMEDIC-LEVEL ADVANCED LIFE SUPPORT (ALS) COVERAGE, AND MODERN AMBULANCE INFRASTRUCTURE. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE HIRING THREE (3) FULL-TIME EMS PERSONNEL TO PROVIDE CONTINUOUS EMERGENCY RESPONSE COVERAGE FROM GOLDFIELD USING A 48/96 A-B-C SHIFT SCHEDULE; EXECUTING A CONTRACT WITH RURAL MEDEVAC ALLIANCE TO PROVIDE A DEDICATED 24/7 PARAMEDIC QUICK RESPONSE SERVICE VEHICLE (QRV) THAT RESPONDS TO ALL 911 CALLS COUNTYWIDE AND SUPPORTS PATIENT CARE DURING TRANSPORT; PURCHASING AND PLACING INTO SERVICE THREE (3) NEW TYPE I AMBULANCES STATIONED IN GOLDFIELD, SILVER PEAK, AND FISH LAKE VALLEY (DYER); IMPLEMENTING COORDINATED DISPATCH, RESPONSE, AND PATIENT CARE PROTOCOLS; AND PROVIDING ONGOING EMS TRAINING AND CONTINUING EDUCATION TO STRENGTHEN LOCAL WORKFORCE CAPACITY. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO ESTABLISH DATA COLLECTION AND PERFORMANCE MONITORING SYSTEMS TO EVALUATE SERVICE UTILIZATION, RESPONSE TIMES, STAFFING, AND PATIENT OUTCOMES AND TO GUIDE FUTURE EXPANSION OF THE COUNTY’S EMS SYSTEM.

name: NORTHERN NYE COUNTY HOSPITAL DISTRICT
description: NORTHERN NYE COUNTY HOSPITAL DISTRICT (NNCHD) WILL EXPAND AND STRENGTHEN EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES THROUGHOUT NORTHERN NYE COUNTY BY ESTABLISHING A PROFESSIONALLY STAFFED, 24/7 EMS RESPONSE MODEL SERVING TONOPAH, ROUND MOUNTAIN, AND SURROUNDING RURAL AND FRONTIER COMMUNITIES. THE PROJECT ADDRESSES SIGNIFICANT GAPS IN EMERGENCY RESPONSE CAPACITY CAUSED BY THE REGION’S VAST GEOGRAPHY, LONG TRANSPORT DISTANCES, LIMITED LOCAL HEALTHCARE INFRASTRUCTURE, AGING AMBULANCE RESOURCES, AND HISTORIC RELIANCE ON A SMALL VOLUNTEER EMS WORKFORCE. NORTHERN NYE COUNTY ENCOMPASSES APPROXIMATELY 11,685 SQUARE MILES AND HAS FEWER THAN 6,000 RESIDENTS. THE REGION HAS NO LOCAL HOSPITAL OR EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT, AND PATIENTS REQUIRING HOSPITAL-LEVEL CARE MUST GENERALLY BE TRANSPORTED MORE THAN ONE HOUR, WITH TRAUMA-LEVEL CARE REQUIRING TRAVEL OF MORE THAN TWO HOURS ONE WAY. AMBULANCE TRANSPORTS CAN REMOVE A UNIT FROM LOCAL SERVICE FOR AS LONG AS SIX HOURS, SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCING EMERGENCY RESPONSE CAPACITY FOR THE REMAINING SERVICE AREA. NNCHD WILL COMPETITIVELY PROCURE THE EMS PROVIDER DURING THE INITIAL TWO MONTHS OF THE PROJECT PERIOD, WITH CONTRACTED SERVICE IMPLEMENTATION AND PERSONNEL DEPLOYMENT TO FOLLOW UPON COMPLETION OF THE PROCUREMENT PROCESS. DURING THE OCTOBER 1, 2026 THROUGH AUGUST 30, 2027 PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE, NNCHD WILL CONTRACT WITH AN EMS PROVIDER TO ESTABLISH CONTINUOUS PROFESSIONAL AMBULANCE STAFFING IN BOTH TONOPAH AND ROUND MOUNTAIN. TWO AMBULANCE UNITS WILL BE STAFFED 24 HOURS PER DAY, SEVEN DAYS PER WEEK BY A TOTAL OF 12 EMT-LEVEL PROFESSIONALS, WITH SIX PERSONNEL SUPPORTING EACH LOCATION. PERSONNEL WILL RESPOND NOT ONLY WITHIN THEIR PRIMARY STATION AREAS BUT THROUGHOUT NORTHERN NYE COUNTY AS NEEDED. NNCHD WILL SUPPORT RECRUITMENT OF QUALIFIED EMS PROFESSIONALS, INCLUDING CURRENT VOLUNTEER RESPONDERS INTERESTED IN TRANSITIONING TO PAID POSITIONS, WHILE THE CONTRACTED EMS PROVIDER WILL EMPLOY, ONBOARD, ADMINISTER, AND SUPERVISE THE WORKFORCE. EMT-LEVEL PERSONNEL WILL ALSO BE ENCOURAGED TO PURSUE ADVANCED EMT TRAINING TO INCREASE THE NUMBER OF LOCALLY AVAILABLE ADVANCED PROVIDERS AND STRENGTHEN THE REGION’S LONG-TERM EMS WORKFORCE. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO ESTABLISH ONE 24/7 AEMT-LEVEL SUPERVISORY POSITION STAFFED BY THREE PROFESSIONALS. THIS POSITION WILL PROVIDE SCHEDULING AND OPERATIONAL COORDINATION, CLINICAL OVERSIGHT, PROTOCOL COMPLIANCE, PERFORMANCE MONITORING, COORDINATION WITH VOLUNTEER RESPONDERS AND REGIONAL HEALTHCARE PARTNERS, AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT. THE SUPERVISOR WILL SERVE AS THE PRIMARY OPERATIONAL CONTACT BETWEEN THE CONTRACTED EMS PROVIDER AND NNCHD AND WILL HELP ENSURE CONSISTENT STANDARDS OF CARE ACROSS THE EXPANDED EMS SYSTEM. THE EXPANDED SERVICE WILL BUILD UPON NNCHD’S EXISTING LOCALLY FUNDED PARTNERSHIP WITH REMSA HEALTH, WHICH CURRENTLY PROVIDES ONE 24/7 PARAMEDIC-LEVEL POSITION BASED IN TONOPAH AND OPERATING A QUICK RESPONSE VEHICLE (QRV). THE PARAMEDIC/QRV PROVIDES ADVANCED EMERGENCY INTERVENTION AND CAN RESPOND EVEN WHEN AN AMBULANCE IS UNAVAILABLE BECAUSE OF A LONG-DISTANCE TRANSPORT. THE RHT-FUNDED EXPANSION WILL ADD STAFFED AMBULANCE CAPACITY AND SYSTEMWIDE SUPERVISION WHILE INTEGRATING WITH THIS EXISTING PARAMEDIC RESOURCE TO CREATE A MORE RELIABLE AND COORDINATED EMS RESPONSE SYSTEM. THE PROJECT WILL FURTHER IMPROVE EMS READINESS THROUGH THE ACQUISITION AND DEPLOYMENT OF TWO NEW TYPE I AMBULANCES, ONE ASSIGNED TO TONOPAH AND ONE TO ROUND MOUNTAIN, TOGETHER WITH UPDATED MEDICAL AND COMMUNICATIONS EQUIPMENT NECESSARY TO SUPPORT SAFE EMERGENCY RESPONSE AND TRANSPORT. EQUIPMENT WILL INCLUDE POWER-LOAD STRETCHERS, CARDIAC MONITORS, VENTILATORS, STAIR CHAIRS, RADIOS, IPADS, MOBILE DATA TERMINALS, MODEMS, COMPUTERS, AND RELATED EMS EQUIPMENT. THE CONTRACTED EMS PROVIDER WILL ALSO PROVIDE THE DISPATCH, COMMUNICATIONS, LOGISTICS, DATA MANAGEMENT, QUALITY ASSURANCE, AND ADMINISTRATIVE INFRASTRUCTURE NECESSARY TO SUPPORT THE EXPANDED SYSTEM.

description: MINERAL COUNTY EMS WILL MODERNIZE ITS EMERGENCY MEDICAL FLEET AND CLINICAL CAPABILITY TO CLOSE A DOCUMENTED GAP IN HIGH-ACUITY, “TREAT-IN-PLACE” AND STABILIZED RURAL TRANSPORT CARE. MINERAL COUNTY EMS’S RESPONSE AREA ENCOMPASSES THE ENTIRE COUNTY, AND THE DEPARTMENT TYPICALLY TRANSPORTS PATIENTS TO MT. GRANT GENERAL HOSPITAL, WITH OCCASIONAL TRANSPORTS TO FALLON, RENO, OR CARSON CITY FOR A HIGHER LEVEL OF CARE; ONE-WAY TRANSPORT DISTANCES RANGE FROM 1 TO 250 MILES. THE DEPARTMENT’S FLEET INCLUDES TWO AMBULANCES THAT HAVE REACHED THE END OF THEIR RELIABLE SERVICE LIFE: A 2002 FORD F-350 AMBULANCE STATIONED IN MINA, FOR WHICH REPLACEMENT PARTS ARE NO LONGER AVAILABLE, AND A 2012 MERCEDES SPRINTER AMBULANCE WITH 145,800 MILES. PATIENT-LIFT SYSTEMS ARE CURRENTLY INSTALLED IN THESE UNITS, BUT THE LIFTS ARE 14 YEARS OLD AND ARE DUE FOR REPLACEMENT. THROUGH THIS SUBAWARD, MINERAL COUNTY WILL (1) PROCURE AND PLACE INTO SERVICE TWO NEW WHEELED COACH TYPE 1 AMBULANCES (ONE 4X4 AND ONE 4X2) TO REPLACE THE 2002 FORD F-350 MINA UNIT AND THE 2012 SPRINTER, EACH EQUIPPED WITH NEW STRYKER POWER-LOAD NO-LIFT SYSTEMS TO REPLACE THE EXISTING 14-YEAR-OLD LIFTS, (2) PROCURE AND DEPLOY ADVANCED DIAGNOSTIC AND RESPIRATORY EQUIPMENT—INCLUDING THE HEROVENT TRANSPORT VENTILATOR, VSCAN AIR ULTRASOUND, POCKET-DOP, AND DIGITAL STETHOSCOPES—AND TRAIN ALL FIELD STAFF TO FULL PROFICIENCY IN THEIR USE, AND (3) BUILD A SUSTAINABLE, “GROW-YOUR-OWN” REGIONAL CLINICAL WORKFORCE PIPELINE THROUGH IN-HOUSE TRAINING, ADVANCING EMT-BASICS TO ADVANCED EMT (AEMT) LEVEL—MINERAL COUNTY EMS DOES NOT STAFF PARAMEDICS—WITH COURSE SEATS EXTENDED TO COMMUNITY RECRUITS FROM MINERAL COUNTY AND NEIGHBORING RURAL/FRONTIER COMMUNITIES THAT LACK LOCAL TRAINING CAPACITY, INCLUDING ESMERALDA COUNTY AND GABBS (NYE COUNTY), AND CERTIFYING STAFF IN WILDERNESS MEDICINE AND FARMEDIC RESPONSE. BASELINE METRICS: MINERAL COUNTY CURRENTLY OPERATES A 2002 FORD F-350 AMBULANCE STATIONED IN MINA FOR WHICH REPLACEMENT PARTS ARE NO LONGER AVAILABLE, AND A 2012 SPRINTER AMBULANCE WITH 145,800 MILES. BOTH UNITS HAVE PATIENT-LIFT SYSTEMS INSTALLED, BUT THOSE LIFTS ARE 14 YEARS OLD. THE DEPARTMENT HAS NO ONBOARD ADVANCED TRANSPORT VENTILATOR OR POINT-OF-CARE ULTRASOUND CAPABILITY, AND A LIMITED NUMBER OF STAFF ARE CREDENTIALED ABOVE THE EMT-BASIC. PROVIDER LIFT-RELATED INJURY INCIDENCE AND ALS-LEVEL BILLING CAPTURE ARE TRACKED BUT CURRENTLY LIMITED BY THE AGING FLEET, AGING LIFT EQUIPMENT, AND STAFFING GAPS DESCRIBED ABOVE. PROJECTED OUTCOME METRICS: BY THE END OF BUDGET PERIOD 1, MINERAL COUNTY PROJECTS: THE 2002 FORD F-350 MINA AMBULANCE AND THE 2012 SPRINTER (145,800 MILES) FULLY REPLACED BY TWO NEW TYPE 1 AMBULANCES (4X4 AND 4X2) IN DAILY SERVICE, EACH WITH A NEW STRYKER POWER-LOAD SYSTEM REPLACING THE 14-YEAR-OLD LIFTS, AND A MEASURABLE REDUCTION IN LIFT-RELATED STAFF INJURIES RELATIVE TO BASELINE; 100% OF FIELD STAFF PROFICIENT IN THE USE OF THE HEROVENT, VSCAN AIR, POCKET-DOP, AND DIGITAL STETHOSCOPES, VERIFIED THROUGH BI-MONTHLY HIGH-FIDELITY SIMULATIONS; AN INCREASED NUMBER OF STAFF HOLDING AEMT CREDENTIALS THROUGH IN-HOUSE TRAINING (MINERAL COUNTY EMS DOES NOT STAFF PARAMEDICS).

name: MT GRANT GENERAL HOSPITAL
description: THIS PROJECT WILL FOCUS RENOVATING THE RADIOLOGY DEPARTMENT SPACE TO HOUSE EQUIPMENT (THE PHILIPS RADIOGRAPHY 7300 C WITH AMBIENT LIGHTING SYSTEM) PURCHASED UNDER A PRIVATE SECTOR GRANT AWARD FROM THE LEONA M. AND HARRY B. HELMSLEY CHARITABLE TRUST. CURRENTLY, MGGH RELIES ON A 1993 BENNETT RADIOLOGY UNIT, WHICH NO LONGER HAS PARTS AVAILABLE, PLUS ITS OBSOLETE STATUS HAS MADE IT INCREASINGLY DIFFICULT TO SERVICE OVER THE LAST TWO YEARS. IN CONTRAST, THE PHILIPS RADIOGRAPHY 7300 C IS A SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER PERFORMANCE UNIT, WITH GREATER IMAGE CLARITY, AS WELL AS INTEGRATION WITH EMR AND TECHNOLOGY DEVICES FOR FACILITATING COLLABORATIVE CARE. NOTABLY, THE AMBIENT LIGHTING SYSTEM WILL HELP TO EASE FEARS AND ANXIETIES BY PATIENTS, INCLUDING THOSE WITH BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DISORDERS, AUTISM, AND OTHER CONDITIONS, WHO FIND CHANGES IN ROUTINES, AND MEDICAL ENCOUNTERS TO BE STRESSORS. REPEAT IMAGES WILL BE REDUCED BY USING THE PHILIPS RADIOGRAPHY 7300 C, WHILE ENSURING A CALM ENVIRONMENT WITH ITS AMBIENT LIGHTING SYSTEM. FURTHER, EXAM TIMES WILL BE REDUCED, THE POSITIONING PROCESS WILL BE EASIER, AND DIAGNOSTIC CONFIDENCE WILL BE ENHANCED WITH GREATER RELIABILITY. IT IS PARAMOUNT THAT THE NEWLY PURCHASED UNIT BE HOUSED WITHIN THE RADIOLOGY DEPARTMENT, AS THE ALTERNATIVE WOULD BE TO TRANSPORT PATIENTS OUTSIDE OF THE HOSPITAL FACILITY TO ANOTHER BUILDING AND EXPOSE THEM TO THE ELEMENTS.

name: NEVADA SYSTEM OF HIGHER EDUCATION
business_types: US STATE GOVERNMENT,STATE CONTROLLED INSTITUTION OF HIGHER LEARNING,EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTION
description: GREAT BASIN COLLEGE (GBC) WILL RENOVATE AND FURNISH SIX EXISTING APARTMENTS ON THE GBC-ELKO CAMPUS TO PROVIDE MOVE-IN-READY HOUSING FOR MEDICAL STUDENTS, PHYSICIAN RESIDENTS, NURSING STUDENTS, ALLIED HEALTH STUDENTS, AND OTHER HEALTHCARE TRAINEES COMPLETING RURAL CLINICAL ROTATIONS IN NORTHEASTERN NEVADA. THE PROJECT ADDRESSES A PRACTICAL BUT SIGNIFICANT BARRIER TO EXPANDING RURAL CLINICAL TRAINING: THE LIMITED AVAILABILITY OF AFFORDABLE, FURNISHED, SHORT-TERM HOUSING FOR TRAINEES COMING TO ELKO COUNTY. DURING THE PROJECT PERIOD, GBC WILL RENOVATE BUILDING A OF THE COLLEGE PARKWAY APARTMENTS, WHICH INCLUDES THREE THREE-BEDROOM AND THREE TWO-BEDROOM UNITS. EACH APARTMENT IS APPROXIMATELY 615 SQUARE FEET AND INCLUDES A KITCHEN, BATHROOM, LIVING SPACE, AND LAUNDRY AREA. GBC WILL COMPETITIVELY PROCURE A LICENSED GENERAL CONTRACTOR TO COMPLETE THE WORK. RENOVATIONS WILL INCLUDE INTERIOR PAINTING AND FLOORING; LIGHTING UPGRADES; KITCHEN AND BATHROOM IMPROVEMENTS; CABINETRY AND COUNTERTOPS; DOORS AND HARDWARE; PLUMBING AND HVAC IMPROVEMENTS; AND EXTERIOR IMPROVEMENTS, INCLUDING STUCCO, TRIM, WINDOWS, AND GUTTERS. FOLLOWING RENOVATION, GBC WILL PURCHASE AND INSTALL THE FURNITURE, APPLIANCES, FIXTURES, AND HOUSEHOLD ITEMS NEEDED TO MAKE ALL SIX UNITS FULLY FURNISHED AND READY FOR OCCUPANCY. GREAT BASIN COLLEGE WILL ALSO WORK WITH ITS HEALTHCARE AND ACADEMIC PARTNERS TO COORDINATE CLINICAL ROTATION SCHEDULES AND HOUSING NEEDS. PARTNERS INCLUDE NORTHEASTERN NEVADA REGIONAL HOSPITAL (NNRH), NEVADA HEALTH CENTERS (NVHC), THE UNIVERSITY OF NEVADA, RENO (UNR), THE UNIVERSITY OF NEVADA, LAS VEGAS (UNLV), NEVADA STATE UNIVERSITY (NSU), AND OTHER HEALTHCARE AND ACADEMIC PARTNERS AS OPPORTUNITIES DEVELOP. THE COMPLETED APARTMENTS WILL PRIMARILY HOUSE HEALTHCARE TRAINEES COMPLETING CLINICAL ROTATIONS IN ELKO AND SURROUNDING RURAL COMMUNITIES. WHEN SPACE IS AVAILABLE, THEY MAY ALSO PROVIDE TEMPORARY HOUSING FOR LICENSED HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS RELOCATING TO THE AREA OR TRAVELING MEDICAL STAFF. THE HEALTHCARE OUTCOME OF THIS PROJECT EXTENDS BEYOND THE RENOVATION OF SIX APARTMENTS. BY PROVIDING RELIABLE HOUSING FOR HEALTHCARE TRAINEES, GBC AND ITS PARTNERS WILL REMOVE AN IDENTIFIED BARRIER TO RURAL CLINICAL PLACEMENTS AND INCREASE THE REGION’S CAPACITY TO EXPOSE FUTURE HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS TO RURAL PRACTICE. THIS INVESTMENT WILL SUPPORT A STRONGER PIPELINE OF PHYSICIANS, NURSES, ADVANCED PRACTICE PROVIDERS, AND ALLIED HEALTH PROFESSIONALS WITH DIRECT EXPERIENCE SERVING RURAL NEVADA. OVER TIME, INCREASING THE NUMBER OF HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS WHO TRAIN IN NORTHEASTERN NEVADA WILL SUPPORT PROVIDER RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION AND IMPROVE ACCESS TO PRIMARY, PREVENTIVE, AND SPECIALTY HEALTHCARE SERVICES THROUGHOUT THE REGION.

description: THIS PROJECT BUILDS UPON EXISTING HEALTH CENTER PROGRAM INFRASTRUCTURE IN NYE COUNTY TO EXPAND THE RANGE AND SCOPE OF PREVENTATIVE CARE SERVICES AVAILABLE IN THE COUNTY'S RURAL COMMUNITIES. SAFE HARBOR MEDICAL (SHM) IS A FEDERALLY QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTER LOOK-ALIKE THAT SERVES SOUTHERN NEVADA AT ITS FULL-SERVICE MEDICAL CENTER IN NYE COUNTY OFFERING PRIMARY CARE, CHIROPRACTIC CARE, WOMEN'S HEALTH, PEDIATRICS, SCHOOL-BASED HEALTH SERVICES, FUNCTIONAL MEDICINE, MENTAL HEALTH AND SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER TREATMENT, NUTRITION COUNSELING, INSURANCE ENROLLMENT ASSISTANCE, AND WRAPAROUND CARE. OPENED IN 2025, THE SITE IN RURAL PAHRUMP PARTNERS WITH NYE COUNTY SCHOOLS TO PROVIDE BACK-TO-SCHOOL PHYSICALS AND IMMUNIZATIONS AT LOW- OR NO-COST, HELPING EXPAND ACCESS TO CARE FOR FAMILIES FACING FINANCIAL AND SOCIAL BARRIERS. SHM ALSO PARTNERS WITH NYE COUNTY JAIL TO OFFER REENTRY SERVICES COORDINATING MEDICAL CARE WITH SUPPORTIVE SERVICES FOR INDIVIDUALS WHO ARE REENTERING THE COMMUNITY POST-INCARCERATION. THE PROJECT INCLUDES TWO NECESSARY AREAS OF FOCUS: (1) SHM WILL CREATE NEW HEALTH CENTER ACCESS POINTS BY MOBILIZING A COMBINED MEDICAL/DENTAL MOBILE UNIT TO REACH RURAL AND FRONTIER COMMUNITIES, AND (2) SHM WILL ADVANCE THE LEVEL OF COMPREHENSIVE CARE AVAILABLE BY ADDING THE CAPACITY TO PROVIDE OCULAR SCREENINGS, RADIOLOGY SERVICES, PRENATAL CARE, AND DENTAL SERVICES. IT ALSO BUILDS UPON EXISTING COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS WITH SERVICE PROVIDERS WHO ARE ALREADY EMBEDDED IN THE TARGET RURAL COMMUNITIES. THROUGH ITS PARTNERS' SITES AND LOCAL COMMUNITY NETWORKS, SHM WILL BE ABLE TO PROVIDE A REGULAR SCHEDULE OF PRIMARY CARE AND DENTAL SERVICES THROUGH THE MOBILE UNIT IN COMMUNITIES THAT DO NOT CURRENTLY HAVE ACCESS TO DENTAL CARE PROVIDERS AND/OR HAVE LIMITED ACCESS TO PRIMARY AND PREVENTATIVE CARE SHM WILL INVEST IN MEDICAL TECHNOLOGY AVAILABLE IN THE COMMUNITY FOR EARLY DIAGNOSIS OF CHRONIC AND ACUTE CONDITIONS THROUGH INFRASTRUCTURAL INVESTMENTS IN THE LEVEL OF CARE OFFERED THROUGH ITS NYE COUNTY MEDICAL CENTER, LOCATED IN PAHRUMP (I.E. THE ADDITION OF DIAGNOSTIC RADIOLOGY, PRENATAL CARE, AND OCULAR SCREENING CAPABILITIES FOR UNDERINSURED/UNINSURED COMMUNITIES). PARTNERS IN THE PROGRAM INCLUDE NYE COUNTY SCHOOLS, TONOPAH CONVENTION CENTER, BEATTY COMMUNITY CENTER, GABBS FIRE SERVICES, AND MANHATTAN FIRE SERVICES, ALL OF WHICH HAVE EXISTING PARTNERSHIPS WITH SHM AND HAVE EXPRESSED INTENT TO SUPPORT CARE EXPANSION ACROSS RURAL NYE COUNTY THROUGH THE ADDITION OF A NEW MOBILE HEALTH UNIT. THE PROGRAM WILL ACHIEVE TWO KEY EXPANSIONS IN NYE COUNTY RURAL HEALTH: (1) THE PROJECT WILL MOBILIZE ON COMBINED MEDICAL/DENTAL MOBILE HEALTH UNIT TO SERVE RURAL COMMUNITIES ACROSS NYE COUNTY WHICH CURRENTLY LACK ACCESS TO BOTH SERVICE LINES, AND (2) THE PROJECT WILL EXPAND THE RANGE OF HEALTH SERVICES AVAILABLE TO THE COMMUNITIES SERVED BY FQHCS (E.G. SHM EXPECTS TO PROVIDE AT LEAST 500 PATIENT VISTS WITH THE MOBILE HEALTH UNIT PURCHASED FOR THIS PROJECT.

description: OHIO'S RURAL HEALTH TRANSFORMATION PROJECT WILL IMPLEMENT INITIATIVES TO IMPROVE HEALTH FOR RURAL OHIOANS THROUGH INNOVATION, HEALTHCARE ACCESS, AND PREVENTION. - THE OHIO RURAL HEALTH TRANSFORMATION PROGRAM (RHTP) PRESENTS THIS PLAN TO STRENGTHEN HEALTHCARE ACCESS, OUTCOMES, AND WORKFORCE CAPACITY ACROSS OHIO’S 73 NON-URBAN COUNTIES. THE 4.4 MILLION RESIDENTS LIVING IN THESE RURAL COMMUNITIES ARE IMPACTED BY LIMITED ACCESS TO CARE, HOSPITAL CLOSURES, WORKFORCE SHORTAGES, AND HIGH RATES OF CHRONIC AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS. RURAL AND APPALACHIAN OHIOANS EXPERIENCE HIGHER RATES OF HEART DISEASE, DIABETES, COPD, CANCER, AND SUICIDE THAN STATE AVERAGES. THIRTEEN COUNTIES ARE MATERNITY CARE DESERTS, AND NEARLY ONE IN FIVE RURAL HOSPITALS IS AT RISK OF CLOSURE. PROVIDER SHORTAGES ARE WIDESPREAD: PRIMARY CARE AVAILABILITY IS NEARLY HALF THAT OF URBAN REGIONS, AND BEHAVIORAL AND ORAL HEALTH GAPS PERSIST. THESE CHALLENGES ARE COMPOUNDED BY LOWER EDUCATION LEVELS, HIGHER POVERTY, AND AN AGING POPULATION—ONE IN THREE RURAL OHIOANS IS OVER AGE 60. OHIO’S PLAN ALIGNS WITH FEDERAL PRIORITIES TO MAKE RURAL AMERICA HEALTHY AGAIN THROUGH SUSTAINABLE ACCESS, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, INNOVATIVE CARE, AND TECH ADVANCEMENT. KEY INITIATIVES: RURAL HEALTH INNOVATION HUBS – ESTABLISH CLINICALLY INTEGRATED NETWORKS (CINS) AND REGIONAL CENTERS OF EXCELLENCE LINKING HOSPITALS, CLINICS, EMS, PHARMACISTS, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS TO COORDINATE CARE, REDUCE COSTS, AND EXPAND CAPACITY. LEGISLATIVE REFORMS WILL ALLOW LOW-RISK BIRTHING CENTERS IN RURAL HOSPITALS. EMERGENCY CARE TRANSFORMATION – SCALE A SUCCESSFUL PILOT ENABLING EMS TO PROVIDE TREAT-IN-PLACE OR ALTERNATE-DESTINATION CARE, REDUCING UNNECESSARY EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT USE THROUGH TRAINING, SYSTEM UPGRADES, AND IMPROVED CONNECTIVITY. SCHOOL-BASED HEALTH CENTERS – ESTABLISH CLINICS ON K–12 AND COLLEGE CAMPUSES OFFERING PRIMARY, BEHAVIORAL, DENTAL, AND TELEHEALTH SERVICES FOR STUDENTS AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS, SERVING ALSO AS RURAL CLINICAL TRAINING SITES. OH SEE – EXPAND STATEWIDE MOBILE VISION, HEARING, AND DENTAL CARE BASED ON A 13-COUNTY PILOT TO ENSURE EARLY DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT FOR CHILDREN. RURAL WORKFORCE PIPELINE – BUILD A CONTINUUM FROM HIGH SCHOOL THROUGH PROFESSIONAL TRAINING AND EMPLOYMENT, FEATURING UPSKILLING FOR COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKERS AND PHARMACISTS, FIVE-YEAR RURAL SERVICE COMMITMENTS, AND PARTNERSHIPS AMONG SCHOOLS, UNIVERSITIES, AND EMPLOYERS. CROSS-CUTTING STRATEGIES: RHTP EMBEDS TELEHEALTH, REMOTE MONITORING, AND INTEROPERABLE ELECTRONIC MEDICAL RECORDS ACROSS INITIATIVES. POLICY ACTIONS INCLUDE EXPANDING PHARMACIST SCOPE OF PRACTICE, ESTABLISHING RURAL BIRTHING CENTERS, REINSTATING THE PRESIDENTIAL FITNESS TEST, AND REQUIRING PHYSICIAN NUTRITION CME. MORE THAN 300 PARTNERS (HOSPITALS, FQHCS, UNIVERSITIES, EMS, ASSOCIATIONS) COLLABORATED ON THE PLAN. IMPLEMENTATION WILL OCCUR THROUGH LOCAL PARTNERS WITH STATE OVERSIGHT. SUSTAINABILITY: EACH PROJECT IS DESIGNED FOR LONG-TERM VIABILITY THROUGH BILLABLE SERVICE MODELS, SHARED-SERVICE EFFICIENCIES, AND ALIGNMENT WITH MEDICAID AND VALUE-BASED PAYMENT SYSTEMS. WORKFORCE INCENTIVES, TECHNOLOGY ADOPTION, AND LEGISLATIVE REFORMS WILL ENSURE CONTINUITY BEYOND THE GRANT PERIOD. EXPECTED OUTCOMES BY 2031: • ESTABLISH REGIONAL INTEGRATED NETWORKS ACROSS ALL RURAL COUNTIES.
